NOSCAL Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan. 3rd Floor, Municipal Hall, 'Talolong Lopez, Quezon Dear Mr. Noscal: S. 20 This has reference to your letter dated 7 February 2019, seeking clarification from this Department the following issues: Is the argument raised by the movant that the given resolution is not subject for opposition or objection leading to the declaration by the Temporary Presiding Officer (T PO) in the approval of the resolution sans calling ibr the division of the house in view of the manifestation of objection to the proposed motion, a valid position? ii. Is the refusal of the TPO to sign the resolution which he declared as "approved", albeit recalled unsuccessfully, makes him liable for any administrative offense? iii. Is the TPO correct in his claim that there should be a division of the house since there was an objection to the proposed motion? iv. Considering that the proposed motion was seconded by one O) member only and there was a manifestation of objection by another member of the municipal legislative council but the TPO failed to call for the division oi the house, is the vote of simple majority, which is required on the approval 01' the given proposed resolution as provided in Article 107, first sentence of paragraph (g) of the IRR of the LGC and in Sec. 15 of the IRP of the Sangguniang of Lopez, met and satisfied that will compel the TPO to certify the approval of (he given resolution as mandated in Section 49(b) of RA 7160 and in Article 102(c) the IRR of the LGC? Query nos. 1 and 2 will be answered in one discussion since they are interrelated to each other.

Foremost, local legislative power is exercised by the sangguniang bayan for the municipality'. Sanggunian is a collegial body, where, legislation, which is the principal function and duty of the sanggunian, requires the participation of its members so that they may not only represent the interests of their respective consticuents but also help in the making of decisions by voting upon every question put upon the body2. Since the herein queries pertains to the passage of a resolution, the same should undergo legislative process to be exercised by the sanggunian concerned as resolutions are also enacted, albeit of temporary nature. If there is/are any objectionß, the same should be reflected in the vote and it is our view that division of the house would be the remedy, where majority vote should always prevail, unless, there are provisions in the internal rules of procedure (IRP) relative to the matter. Hence, the argument raised by the movant in query no. I is not correct and the temporary presiding officer (T PO) is correct in his claim that there should be a division of the house since there was an objection to the proposed motion (query no. 3). This Department is consistent in its opinion that the duty LD certify mentioned in the second part of Section 49(b) is appertaining to a Presiding Officer such that whoever presides over the session would be the one to certify the enacted ordinance/adopted resolution. Section 49(b) explicitly provides that the Presiding Officer shall certify within ten (IO) days from the passage of ordinances enacted and resoluvions adopted by the sanggunian in the session over which he temporarily presided. Certification is defined as the formal assertion in writing 01 some fact. To certify, therefore, is to authenticate or vouch for a thing in writing and to attest to it as being true or as represented. After certification by the Presiding Officer, we are of the view that the ordinances and resolutions subject thereof may already be released. Thus, With respect to query no. 2, we believe that the said TPO may be held liable for dereliction of duty, which is an administrative offense pursuant to Sections 60(c)3 and 61 (b)4 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code". Section 48 of Republic Act No. 7160, or the "Local Government Code" Case of Zamora vs. Caballero, et.al, G.R. No. 147767 dated 14 January 2004 Section 60. Accordingly, query no. 4 should be answered in the affirmative. We hope to have sufficiently assisted you on the matter. Very truly vours, By Authority of iåe Secretary: MARIVEL C.
